output:

```{r setup, include=FALSE}
library(flexdashboard)
library(sf)
library(dplyr)
library(readr)
library(ggplot2)
library(plotly)
library(leaflet)
library(DT)
library(tigris)
library(shiny)
library(lubridate)
options(tigris_use_cache = TRUE)
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE, warning = FALSE, message = FALSE)

# New England state FIPS codes
ne_fips <- c(CT = 9, ME = 23, MA = 25, NH = 33, RI = 44, VT = 50)

raw <- read_csv("data/accident.csv") |>
  filter(STATE %in% ne_fips)

##Builds date and "what was hit" categories

hit_levels <- c("Another vehicle", "Pedestrian or cyclist", "Tree",
                "Pole or sign", "Guardrail or barrier", "Rollover", "Other")

pts <- raw |>
  filter(!is.na(LATITUDE), LATITUDE < 70, LONGITUD < 0) |>
  mutate(
    date   = as.Date(sprintf("%04d-%02d-%02d", YEAR, MONTH, DAY)),
    state  = STATENAME,
    county = tools::toTitleCase(tolower(sub(" \\(\\d+\\)$", "", COUNTYNAME))),
    deaths = factor(ifelse(FATALS == 1, "1 death", "2 or more deaths"),
                    levels = c("1 death", "2 or more deaths")),
    hit = factor(case_when(
      grepl("Pedestrian|Pedalcyclist|Non-Motorist", HARM_EVNAME) ~ "Pedestrian or cyclist",
      grepl("Motor Vehicle", HARM_EVNAME)                        ~ "Another vehicle",
      grepl("Rollover", HARM_EVNAME)                             ~ "Rollover",
      grepl("Tree", HARM_EVNAME)                                 ~ "Tree",
      grepl("Pole|Post|Sign", HARM_EVNAME)                       ~ "Pole or sign",
      grepl("Guardrail|Barrier|Attenuator", HARM_EVNAME)         ~ "Guardrail or barrier",
      TRUE                                                       ~ "Other"),
      levels = hit_levels)
  ) |>
  st_as_sf(coords = c("LONGITUD", "LATITUDE"), crs = 4326, remove = FALSE)

n_dropped <- nrow(raw) - nrow(pts)

# boundaries: outline of the study area
area <- counties(cb = TRUE, year = 2020, progress_bar = FALSE) |>
  filter(STATEFP %in% sprintf("%02d", ne_fips)) |>
  st_transform(4326)

# state outlines (counties dissolved) and the whole study region
ne_states <- area |>
  group_by(STATEFP) |>
  summarise(.groups = "drop") |>
  mutate(state = c("Connecticut", "Maine", "Massachusetts",
                   "New Hampshire", "Rhode Island", "Vermont")[match(as.integer(STATEFP), ne_fips)])

ne_region <- st_make_valid(st_union(area))    

# grey mask: a big box with New England cut out
box <- st_as_sfc(st_bbox(c(xmin = -100, ymin = 30, xmax = -45, ymax = 55),
                         crs = st_crs(4326)))
mask <- st_sf(geometry = st_difference(box, ne_region))

#fixed colors
pal <- colorFactor(c("#EF8A62", "#67001F"), domain = pts$deaths)

all_month <- pts |> st_drop_geometry() |> count(bar = lubridate::floor_date(date, "month"))
all_day   <- pts |> st_drop_geometry() |> count(bar = date)
```

```{r controls}
selectInput("state", "State",
            choices  = c("All New England", sort(unique(pts$state))),
            selected = "All New England")

sliderInput("period", "Dates",
            min = as.Date("2021-01-01"), max = as.Date("2021-12-31"),
            value = c(as.Date("2021-01-01"), as.Date("2021-12-31")),
            step = 1, timeFormat = "%b %d")

checkboxGroupInput("hit", "What was hit first",
                   choices = hit_levels, selected = hit_levels)

radioButtons("unit", "Bars in the chart show",
             choices = c("Months" = "month", "Days" = "day"), inline = TRUE)
```

Pick a state, drag the date handles, and check what the crash hit first and the map, chart, and count will change.

```{r}
chosen <- reactive({
  req(input$state)                      # inputs are empty for an instant at startup
  d <- filter(pts, hit %in% input$hit)  # no req() on hit: nothing ticked = blank map
  if (input$state != "All New England") d <- filter(d, state == input$state)
  d
})

sel <- reactive({
  req(input$period)
  filter(chosen(), between(date, input$period[1], input$period[2]))
})
```

### Fatal crashes selected {.value-box data-height=100}

```{r valuebox}
renderValueBox({
  d <- sel()
  valueBox(nrow(d), icon = "fa-exclamation-triangle",
           caption = sprintf("fatal crashes, %d deaths (%s, %s to %s)",
                             sum(d$FATALS), input$state,
                             format(input$period[1], "%b %d"),
                             format(input$period[2], "%b %d")))
})
```

### Fatal crashes, selected state and dates (one circle per crash)

```{r map}
leafletOutput("map", height = "100%")
```

```{r mapserver}
# Base map: drawn once, reads no input, so the view never resets
output$map <- renderLeaflet({
  leaflet() |>
    addProviderTiles("Esri.WorldStreetMap") |>
    fitBounds(-73.8, 40.9, -66.8, 47.6) |>
    addPolygons(data = mask, stroke = FALSE, fillColor = "grey30",
                fillOpacity = 0.55, options = pathOptions(interactive = FALSE)) |>
    addPolygons(data = area, fill = FALSE, color = "grey55", weight = 1) |>
    addPolygons(data = ne_states, fill = FALSE, color = "grey20", weight = 2.5)
})

# Everything that follows the controls: draws sel() with leafletProxy so the map keeps its zoom
observe({
  req(input$state, input$period)
  d <- sel()
  proxy <- leafletProxy("map") |>
    clearGroup("crashes") |>
    clearGroup("outline") |>
    clearControls()

  if (nrow(d) > 0) {                     # nothing selected -> blank map, no error
    proxy <- proxy |>
      addCircleMarkers(
        data = d, group = "crashes",
        radius = 4, stroke = FALSE, fillOpacity = 0.7, color = ~pal(deaths),
        label = ~sprintf("%s %d, 2021: %d killed (%s County), first hit: %s",
                         MONTHNAME, DAY, FATALS, county, as.character(hit)))
  }

  if (input$state != "All New England") {
    proxy <- proxy |>
      addPolygons(data = filter(ne_states, state == input$state), group = "outline",
                  fill = FALSE, color = "black", weight = 4)
  }

  proxy |>
    addLegend("bottomright", pal = pal, values = pts$deaths, opacity = 0.9,
              title = paste0("Deaths per crash<br>",
                             format(input$period[1], "%b %d"), " to ",
                             format(input$period[2], "%b %d")))
})
```

### Crashes over time

```{r timeseries}
renderPlotly({
  req(input$unit, input$period)
  unit <- input$unit
  w    <- if (unit == "month") 25 else 0.9         # bar width in days
  base <- if (unit == "month") all_month else all_day
  mine <- chosen() |> st_drop_geometry() |>
    count(bar = lubridate::floor_date(date, unit))

  p <- ggplot() +
    annotate("rect", xmin = input$period[1], xmax = input$period[2],
             ymin = -Inf, ymax = Inf, fill = "grey90") +
    geom_col(data = base, aes(bar, n), fill = "grey70", width = w) +
    geom_col(data = mine, aes(bar, n), fill = "#B2182B", width = w) +
    scale_x_date(date_labels = if (unit == "month") "%b" else "%b %d") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = paste("Fatal crashes per", unit)) +
    theme_minimal()

  ggplotly(p)
})
```

> The gray bars represent all of New England while the red bars represent the selected state and the what-was-hit filters. The light band is the selected dates. Over the full year of 2021, crashes were lowest in February and highest in August. There is no population behind the points, so differences reflect where people live and drive the most and not necessarily higher risk per trip.  Daily counts are small so the heights of the bars jump around.  


### About the data {#about}

::: {.about-box}
- **Outcome:** Fatal motor vehicle crashes (a death within 30 days), 2021, one point per crash.
- **Population and method:** There is no population at risk and no expected counts, so these are counts, not risk. Bars show crashes per month or day; the map shows one circle per crash, colored by deaths per crash.
- **Geography:** Six New England states (CT, ME, MA, NH, RI, VT), 67 counties. Points are the coordinates recorded in FARS.
- **Controls:** The reader chooses the state, the dates, and what the crash hit first; the map, chart and count follow.
- **What was hit first:** The first harmful event recorded in FARS, grouped into seven categories (another vehicle, pedestrian or cyclist, tree, pole or sign, guardrail or barrier, rollover, other).
- **Map:** Lighter circles are 1 death, darker circles 2 or more; the unshaded area is the study area.
- **Locations dropped:** 2 of 1,052 crashes have no valid coordinates (coded "not reported") and are not on the map.
- **Areas without data:** 3 of the 67 counties have no fatal crash in the file: Nantucket (MA), Bristol (RI) and Grand Isle (VT). That means no crashes happened, not that data are missing.
- **Limitation:** One year of counts with no population or miles driven, so busier places and roads show more crashes without being riskier. Non-fatal crashes are not in FARS.
- **Source:** NHTSA, Fatality Analysis Reporting System (FARS), 2021 final file, National CSV (https://static.nhtsa.gov/nhtsa/downloads/FARS/2021/National/FARS2021NationalCSV.zip). County boundaries: US Census Bureau, 2020, via `tigris`.
:::
